newsitem.title: UK: Smithkline settles with Medicare for $325 mln.
newsitem.headline: Smithkline settles with Medicare for $325 mln.

text.p: Smithkline Beecham Plc (SB) said on Monday it had reached settlement with various U.S. regulatory bodies regarding disputed claims to Medicare and other government payers from its clinical laboratory unit.
"Under the terms of the settlement, SmithKline Beecham will pay $325 million to resolve the government's civil and administrative claims against the company," SB said in a statement.
The company noted that the payment had been fully provided for within a contingent liabilities reserve announced by SB in March 1996.

Explaining the decision to settle, which Smithkline sought to stress did not mean the company had intentionally violated any laws, chief executive Jan Leschly said the problem had stemmed from ambiguities in regulations and guidlines.
"Although we believe we have strong defences, our decision to settle this case was driven by the enormous potential costs and uncertainties connected with lengthy litigation," he said.
"It was simply too great a risk to our shareholders, employees and customers," he added.
